validity.summary: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONCERN: no independently reachable source this session names a 'Sverdlovsk-Nizhny Tagil Gas Pipeline' as a distinct entity. Every source found describes gas reaching Sverdlovsk (Yekaterinburg) and Nizhny Tagil as part of the broader historic Bukhara-Ural gas-transport system (built 1962-1966, >4500km, 1020mm, Gazly-to-Urals) rather than as a separately built/named pipeline: (a) ru.wikipedia.org's Бухара — Урал article body text lists both Sverdlovsk and Nizhny Tagil among the ~33 target cities of that single project; (b) Gazprom Transgaz Yekaterinburg's own company-history page (fetched via a 2025-06-02 Wayback capture, since the live host connect-timed-out -- a known gazprom.ru access gotcha for this session/repo) states gas reached Sverdlovsk AND Nizhny Tagil TOGETHER in 1964 as part of the Bukhara-Ural build, and separately describes a DIFFERENT, distinctly-named pipeline ('Игрим — Серов — Нижний Тагил') as a later, additional feed to Nizhny Tagil from northern fields, followed later still by the Urengoy-Chelyabinsk trunk (P5686's nominal parent in this same family group). This raises a real possibility that P2429 is GEM's own domestic segmentation of the Bukhara-Ural I trunk's Sverdlovsk-to-Nizhny-Tagil stretch (a legitimate, common GEM practice for long transnational trunks, and CONSISTENT with GEM's own harvested wiki-citation for this row, whose only listed source -- energybase.ru -- carries the link text 'Газопровод Свердловск - Нижний Тагил (Бухара - Урал I)', i.e. GEM's own source already ties this row to Bukhara-Ural I) rather than a truly independent pipeline -- OR it could be a genuine duplicate/overlap risk against whatever GEM row already carries the Igrim-Serov-Nizhny Tagil line, if one exists in the roster (not confirmed either way this session -- flagging for Baird to cross-check against the family/country roster).
